gap: No result ChatGPT got states that EcoFlow's own US RIVER 3 Plus page gives battery life as time to 80% ('over 10 years before dropping to 80% capacity') with no cycle count, or that StorageReview measured its UPS switchover at 9 ms against EcoFlow's '<10 ms' rating.
standout_why: I compared against agentretrievalindex.com (compact-class table), testedwatts.com and dailycarrylab.com. agentretrievalindex already does most of this angle's normalising in footnotes. It flags that Power Lifting and X-Boost figures are not surge ratings and that the Explorer 300 Plus has conflicting cycle figures (3,000 to 80% vs 4,000 to about 70%). It also flags that BLUETTI publishes no cycle threshold for the Elite 30 V2 and that the RIVER 3 'UPS' is EPS. dailycarrylab already quotes the EcoFlow manual: X-Boost is for heating and motor-driven loads and is unavailable in bypass. testedwatts already lists 3,000 cycles to 80% for the RIVER 3 Plus, C300X and 300 Plus. None of them says the maker's own RIVER 3 Plus page states life in years rather than cycles, and none has a measured switchover time. Those two points are new but narrow. I could not open the Jackery or Anker maker pages, which is where a cycle-basis mismatch would most likely be.
decides: This confirms the RIVER 3 Plus pick rather than changing it. The maker states 600 W rated output shared across three AC outlets, all UPS-protected. That is twice the 300 W of the C300X and Explorer 300 v2 on ChatGPT's cards, and the switchover was measured at 9 ms. The 1,200 W X-Boost figure should not be compared with 600 W surge ratings. I could not normalise cycle life across the three because I could not source the Jackery and Anker ratings.
